alex: CI image push is failing on canary after the Dockerfile change (multi-stage). Build job #312 -> push step gets 403. Anyone seen this before?
priya: can you paste the push log?
alex: here ya go:
```
Failed to push image: failed to push remote: unexpected status: 403 Forbidden
Status: 403
Error: denied: requested access to the resource is denied
```
javier: that usually smells like creds or robot account perms. Did we rotate the registry token recently?
sam: I rotated the `robot-builder` token last night for compliance, might be related. Did we update the CI secret?
alex: job uses `docker-registry-creds` secret in namespace `ci-runners`. I didn't touch that. Can someone check the secret value?
priya: you can check with: `kubectl -n ci-runners get secret docker-registry-creds -o yaml` — look for auth field.
alex: ran that, it still references `robot-builder-2022` in the metadata.
javier: okay looks like creds are stale. Quick fix: update secret with the new token and redeploy runner pods so they pick it up. Use `kubectl -n ci-runners delete pod -l app=runner` after updating secret.
sam: updating now. Command I used: `kubectl -n ci-runners create secret docker-registry docker-registry-creds --docker-username=$ROBOT_USER --docker-password=$ROBOT_TOKEN --docker-server=registry.internal.redwood` (with `--dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` to rotate safely).
ci-bot: rerun requested by @sam for job build-image-canary #312
alex: I also want to sanity-check: is it possible the Dockerfile multi-stage change altered the push scope or image name? The job tags images with `canary/$COMMIT_SHA` so should be same repo.
priya: good call — run the previous commit build to confirm it's not the Dockerfile itself. If previous commit pushes fine then it's definitely creds.
ajx: ran a quick local check: pushing the same tag with old creds fails locally once I removed login -> confirms auth.
sam: secret rotated and runners restarted. Kicking off a rerun now.
alex: rerun finished — push succeeded! image digest: `sha256:abc123def456` — confirming canary image is on registry ✅
priya: sweet. For follow-up: let's add an automated check in the CI health pipeline that attempts a tiny authenticated push (or `docker login`) before heavy builds, so we fail fast on creds rotation. Also add a note in the ops runbook to rotate CI secrets when robot tokens are rotated.
javier: also consider using short-lived OIDC tokens for runners so we avoid manual secret syncs.
alex: thanks all — closing this thread. If anyone wants to bisect the multi-stage change later, ping me; but this one was creds-related. :thumbsup:
